column2: the plan defers ci test-harness shard rebalancing to a follow-up even though the issue definition of done requires rebalancing after the g1–g13 bash-harness deletion. if harness targets, counts, or timings change during e3, the makefile shard layout (and related rebalance artifacts) can remain stale while the pr claims the terminal sweep is complete.

the plan's residual bash inventory can admit live sourced terminal libraries (for example `scripts/lib-quiet.sh`, `scripts/lib-net.sh`, and related `lib-*.sh` shared libs) as kept surface rather than requiring zero-consumer deletion. e3 can close while those libs still ship and terminal-lib retirement stays incomplete.

the plan's residual bash inventory and narrowed linter/pre-commit scope omit `.claude/skills/combine-issues/scripts/search-implementing-issue.sh` even though issue scope deliberately keeps it and the combine-issues skill still invokes it. implementing the narrowed residual filters can drop shellcheck, bash-syntax, bash32, and related coverage for that kept executable.

the plan narrows pre-commit shellcheck selection, but `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` still runs shellcheck over every `.sh` under `scripts`, `skills`, and `.claude`. bash-targeting lint scope is therefore inconsistent between local/pre-commit narrowing and ci, so the bash linter surface is not scoped down uniformly.

retired terminal-lib rows are planned without a complete reference-cleanup step. after appending deleted libs to `python/migrated-scripts.tsv`, `make lint-retired-scripts` will flag existing full-path references outside the listed update set, so the required lint gate cannot pass. affected surfaces include script contract docs, skill docs, and literal guards (e.g. `scripts/sessionstart-health.md`, `skills/upgrade-larch/skill.md`, `python/test_upgrade_larch.py`).

the terminal sweep retires `scripts/lib-quiet.sh`, but `scripts/deny-edit-write.sh` still sources it and routes all `block()` deny json through `larch_quiet_init` and `emit()` to fd 3. if `lib-quiet.sh` is deleted without a documented per-hook inline fd-3/stdout emit path, pretooluse deny envelopes for `/research` may fail open or land on the wrong stream, weakening the mechanical read-only-repo contract.

the planned residual bash inventory and compliance pass do not account for `*.inc.bash` files, even though `lint-bash32.sh` already scans them (`git ls-files … '*.sh' '*.inc.bash'`). the repo still has tracked includes (`scripts/oos-disposition-shared.inc.bash`, `scripts/run-log-terminal-outcomes.inc.bash`). e3 could ship with tracked bash include files outside the documented residual inventory and outside the new residual manifest, leaving the terminal sweep incomplete.

the planned residual-bash helper contract has no `--root` or fixture-root parameter, while linter harnesses (`test-lint-bash32.sh`, `test-lint-awk-multibyte-regex.sh`, `test-lint-renderer-substitution-safety.sh`) invoke linters with `--root "$tmproot"` against temp fixture trees. if linters switch to a repo-root manifest reader without preserving that `--root` behavior, fixture scans may ignore the requested root or fail to find fixture manifests.

the plan fully specifies the per-hook fd-3 contract only for `deny-edit-write.sh`. if `lib-quiet.sh` is removed without equivalent per-hook routing, `sessionstart-health.sh` (conditional `larch_quiet_init` / stdout fallback in stripped-path harness runs), `hook-stop-fail-close.sh` (always quiet-inits then `emit()` for stop `decision:block` json), and related hook contract streams break: sessionstart advisories, `make test-sessionstart-health` stdout cases, and post-`/review` halt protection via stop block output.

the plan narrows `lint-awk-multibyte-regex` discovery to residual bash manifest paths, but the manifest only lists `.sh` and `.inc.bash` while the test plan says to preserve standalone `.awk` coverage. implemented literally, standalone `.awk` files stop being scanned or the preserved harness fails.
